title: Bidirectional A* on Austin: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* shrink search time by expanding from both start and goal until the frontiers meet. This visualization mirrors how routing AI can compute efficient paths quickly on real road graphs.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

On a real street graph (nodes = intersections, edges = road segments), Bidirectional A* runs two A* searches at the same time:
• Forward A* from the start
• Backward A* from the goal

Each side uses f(n)=g(n)+h(n), where g(n) is the path cost so far and h(n) is an admissible heuristic (often straight-line distance). The magic is when the two expanding waves meet—then we stitch the best partial paths into the final route.

Why it’s fast:
1) You explore from both ends, so the effective search depth drops.
2) With a good heuristic, each frontier stays focused instead of expanding outward blindly.

Takeaway: If you need optimal paths but want fewer expansions, Bidirectional A* is one of the cleanest graph-search upgrades.

Debate question: Should routing AI prioritize “least time” (weights) or “most reliable” paths (uncertainty-aware costs) first?
